title: How can one angle of a parallelogram give the other three?
description: One angle of a parallelogram is thirty degrees. Each side that cuts a pair of parallel sides gives a pair of angles that add up to one hundred eighty, and this finds the other three angles. Keeko doubts that the angle next to it is sixty degrees.
teaching_notes: One idea: the angles on the same side of a transversal between parallel sides add up to one hundred eighty degrees. Watch for students who subtract from ninety instead of one hundred eighty.

video_script.why: The child sees that every side of a parallelogram cuts a pair of parallel sides, so neighbouring angles add up to 180 degrees.
video_script.substitution: the book's own parallelogram with angle A = 30 degrees
video_script.anchor: the parallelogram ABCD of the book with angle A = 30 degrees
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes thirty from ninety and says angle B is sixty degrees, but neighbouring angles of a parallelogram add up to 180 degrees.
video_script.payoff_line: Angle B and angle D are one hundred fifty degrees each

final_answer.spoken: angle B is one hundred fifty degrees, angle C is thirty degrees, and angle D is one hundred fifty degrees

never_show: angle B as 60 degrees on the board
maths_rules: AB || DC with transversal AD: angle A + angle D = 180
AD || BC with transversal AB: angle A + angle B = 180, so angle B = 180 - 30 = 150
angle C + angle D = 180, so angle C = 180 - 150 = 30
video_script.design: One idea: neighbouring angles between parallel sides add up to 180 degrees. One parallelogram stays on the board and each angle is found in turn.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the parallelogram ABCD with the thirty degree angle at A marked and the other three angles shown as question marks

marks.ang: the thirty degree angle at A is marked
marks.ask: question marks appear at the other three corners

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a parallelogram.
<bookmark mark='ang'/>One of its angles is thirty degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The other three angles are not given.
Do you think they are all thirty degrees too?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two parallel lines cut by a slanting line; the two angles on the same side are marked and joined by a plus sign; the word transversal

marks.line: the slanting line crosses the two parallels
marks.sum: the two angles on the same side are marked and add up to a straight angle

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>A line that cuts two parallel lines is called a transversal.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The two angles on the same side of the transversal add up to one hundred eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eigh B C D is a parallelogram, and angle eigh is thirty degrees.
<bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find angle B, angle C and angle D.

marks.ad: side AD is traced as the transversal
marks.sum1: the two angles on the same side light up

narration: <bookmark mark='ad'/>Step one, eigh B and C D are parallel, and eigh D cuts them.
<bookmark mark='sum1'/>Angle eigh plus angle D is one hundred eighty degrees, because they are on the same side.
<bookmark mark='dv'/>Angle D is one hundred eighty minus thirty, which is one hundred fifty degrees.

marks.ab: side AB is traced as the transversal

narration: <bookmark mark='ab'/>Step two, eigh D and B C are parallel, and eigh B cuts them.
Angle eigh plus angle B is one hundred eighty degrees.
<bookmark mark='bv'/>Angle B is one hundred eighty minus thirty, which is one hundred fifty degrees.

marks.cd: side CD is traced as the transversal
marks.cs: angles C and D light up

narration: <bookmark mark='cd'/>Step three, C D cuts the parallels eigh D and B C.
<bookmark mark='cs'/>Angle C plus angle D is one hundred eighty degrees, because they are on the same side.
<bookmark mark='cv'/>Angle C is one hundred eighty minus one hundred fifty, which is thirty degrees.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, check the four angles.
<bookmark mark='tot'/>Thirty plus one hundred fifty plus thirty plus one hundred fifty is three hundred sixty.
The angles of a four-sided shape add up to three hundred sixty degrees.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Angle B and angle D are one hundred fifty degrees each.
Angle C is thirty degrees.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 30 + 60 = 90 crossed out; the straight line through A and B with the two angles on it

marks.doubt: thirty plus sixty equals ninety appears
marks.wide: corner B glows as wider than a right angle
marks.fix: the two angles are shown on a straight line adding to a straight angle

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks angle B is sixty degrees, because thirty and sixty make ninety.
<bookmark mark='wide'/>But corner B is wider than a right angle.
Angle eigh and angle B sit between parallel sides, on the same side of a transversal.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>They add up to one hundred eighty, not ninety, so angle B is one hundred fifty degrees.
